A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same octic-equivariant ViT work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeiT III and DINOv2 experiments, computational benchmarks, invariantization and block-count ablations, and hematology finetuning results.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds an equivariance control, component runtime measurements, and additional baseline results. The questionable attribution of Table 7 does not negate the other original results.

M1.justification: The stated classification readout changes from global average pooling after invariantization in v1 Section 3.2.3 to extracting the [CLS] token in v3 Section 3.3.3. This is a localized revision of the reported procedure; the octic layers, invariantization choices, and model families remain. The PDFs do not explain whether this reflects an implementation change or a correction to the description.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix E.2 and Table 7 claim additional classification evaluations on iNaturalist2021 and Places365, absent from v1. However, all 24 accuracy entries exactly duplicate the corresponding ImageNet-1K and ADE20K entries in Table 3. The PDFs cannot resolve whether additional evaluations occurred or the table was copied or mislabeled. The established ImageNet, segmentation, rotation-test, and hematology coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 Table 3 adds H2(ViT-H/16) and H2(ViT-L/16) to the DINOv2 comparison; v1 included horizontal-reflection baselines only in the DeiT III comparison. Table 2 also adds evaluated H2 and D2 comparators to the rotation test, replacing four N/A entries. The other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds a ViT-B control using an unconstrained patch embedding while retaining the remaining H8 architecture. Appendix A.2 introduces a separate forward-runtime protocol with batch size 32 and channel widths 256–2048. Existing training budgets, hyperparameter tables, rotation evaluation, and batch-64 throughput protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Section 4.3 adds a targeted control separating enforced equivariance from the retained block-diagonal structure: the unconstrained patch embedding obtains 82.4% versus 83.0% for H8(ViT-B). Appendix A.2 adds component timing analysis across widths, and rotation testing gains additional comparators. The block-count and six-way invariantization ablations already appeared in v1.

E5.justification: The new component timing benchmark explicitly averages 1,000 forward runs. This is separate from the retained throughput protocol averaging 100 runs after 10 warm-up iterations, not an increase in that experiment's repetitions. Neither version supplies training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing main accuracy, segmentation, invariantization, and hematology numbers are retained. Throughput values change: Table 1's ViT-H speedup decreases from 1.57x to 1.47x, while Table 2's baseline ViT-H throughput changes from 526 to 569 images/s. v3 also adds H2 DINOv2 scores, four rotation-test results, the equivariance control, and component timings. Table 7 adds purported benchmark results whose attribution is unresolved because their values duplicate Table 3.

T1.justification: The group representations, equivariance arguments, Fourier matrix, and invariantization formulas are retained. Changing feature orientation and channel notation is mathematically equivalent, and the arithmetic-intensity argument moves to Appendix B. The new FFT runtime subsection explains and benchmarks the existing construction without adding a formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the performance claim from improving accuracy alongside approximately 40% FLOP savings to matching or maintaining accuracy with those savings. v3 also explicitly highlights the two model families and ablation findings as contributions. The central claim that octic equivariance improves computational efficiency remains.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new patch-embedding control as evidence that equivariance contributes beyond block-diagonal structure, and explains the component timing results through small activation overhead versus quadratic linear-layer savings. It attributes poor small-k I8 performance to early invariantization. The limitations retain the principal boundaries but remove v1's explicit prediction that benefits will persist at still larger trained scales.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 documents the new timing benchmark's A100 hardware, batch size, tested dimensions, MLP construction, and repetition count. The existing training hyperparameters, software versions, compute accounting, Fourier implementation listing, and code-release and licensing information are substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 expands comparisons with equivariant transformers and efficient equivariant networks, adding works such as He et al., Rojas-Gomez et al., and several point-cloud transformers. It explicitly contrasts their computational benefits with its own and connects the work to the debate about equivariance at scale. The foundational positioning as an extension of Bökman et al.'s reflection-equivariant approach remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list, and substantial introductory and related-work passages are rewritten. v3 creates a dedicated Octic ViTs subsection, reorganizes experiments so ablations follow the main evaluations, moves arithmetic intensity to an appendix, and restructures appendix headings. These constitute substantial narrative and organizational changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 introduces a linear-layer computation diagram, substantially redraws the architecture figure, moves the group-action visualization from the main text to the appendix, and removes the old separate octic-layer illustration. It adds runtime and additional-benchmark tables, expands comparison tables, and changes the document template and captions. The learned-filter and training-curve figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional equivariance control, closer DINOv2 baselines, component timings, and more restrained accuracy claims improve support and clarity. However, new Table 7 duplicates all 24 accuracy entries from different tasks in Table 3, leaving its claimed generalization evidence unresolved. The redrawn architecture caption also incorrectly identifies k=0 as the all-octic case despite defining k as the number of octic blocks. These reporting problems coexist with useful additions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
